assumptions.request_protocol: RUN high requests continuous cycles. RUN low finishes an already-started cycle, after synchronization latency. A rising debounced STEP while READY and idle sets a pending latch; ACTIVE clears it after acceptance. Holding STEP high does not repeat. STEP during an active cycle is ignored. Raw switch debounce and HALT/CONTINUE arbitration are external to this core.
assumptions.reset_protocol: RESET_IN_n asynchronously aborts the current cycle. Receivers must remain inhibited during reset and until controller initialization. Release only after supply is valid and the oscillator startup interval has elapsed. READY is an internal reset-sequencing indication, not a power-good detector.

unqualified: Oscillator cycle-to-cycle jitter is not bounded in the cited data sheet; 2 ns internal and 10 ns output uncertainty are allocated design limits.
Maximum propagation bounds are used at their data-sheet input-slew and load conditions; source-to-receiver slew compatibility needs electrical modelling or measurements.
Trace capacitance, connector loading and clock routing allocations need extracted PCB evidence.
The asynchronous request and reset entry stages have no metastability MTBF qualification.
Front-panel debounce, HALT/CONTINUE arbitration, power supervisor, receiver reset inhibition and backplane hookup remain to be implemented.
Exact passive parts, distributor availability, footprint review and independent review remain open.

checks.limitation: Pin-derived core, ideal oscillator boundary, asynchronous request with entry-stage metastability excluded. Whole-cycle stop, latched single-step and continuous running are tested. Switch debounce, HALT arbitration, power supervisor and bus integration remain open. conditional bounds, not physical qualification.

models.fidelity: ROM-executed reverse-RLE loader reconstructs the unchanged graphics payload with descending PUSH writes. models.procurement: Physical ROM/flash programming and full-device readback are pending. Host rendering consumes observed IO; display electronics remain unimplemented.

models.fidelity: FR1 private-output flash array and AL2 staged ALU; buffered address and bank-select fanout, two-level AHCT157 bank selection. Normal repository benches enforce flash startup, run operand/continuous/all-opcode profiles and observe complete demo output at ME1 IO pins. Shared DATA, clock/reset, supply startup and private SRAM turnaround remain conditional.
models.procurement: Exact industrial PLCC part is listed in the manufacturer family catalogue. Batronix USB Chip Programmer I support list names the part and BA005 adapter. Physical procurement, programming/readback, socket/passive selection and release review remain open.

models.fidelity: Compiled hello_world and emulator_demo execute from reset through HALT using C1/SQ1/CW1/PC1/AL1/RG1/SP1/MA1/ME1. Every fetch/control cycle is compared. IO connector events and 40 ns setup/hold are checked; host rendering consumes only observed port/data pairs and compares exact text plus source bitmap. Missing, extra and wrong IO event mutations exercise the checks. Device timing remains conditional on unqualified electrical loads.
models.procurement: Fixture-loaded program and zero RAM; bootstrap jump where required. Program loader, display circuit, ALU ROM replacement and physical release remain open.

models.fidelity: KiCad-derived AT27C512R ROM, AS6C1008 SRAM, private data nets, read-source muxes, CPU DATA driver and PH3-captured IO with PH0 strobe. models.procurement: Exact active logic candidates with retained ACT283 source. Stock, passive parts, footprints and independent release review remain open.

models.fidelity: KiCad-derived resettable A, enabled B/function storage, M27C322 ROM, PH1 result snapshot, synchronous PH3 flags and reset-inhibited A/ALU/F drivers. risks.title: ALU identity and physical package allocation
risks.action: All 90 ALU/Memory symbol instances, including power/spare units, the result buffer and flag-feedback buffer, are assigned to 32 explicit packages. The 49 formerly anonymous instances and fifteen copied-value conflicts are resolved. Unit remapping preserves pin endpoints; KiCad independently checks the resulting net groups.

risks.title: Exact parts and ROM programming
risks.action: FR1/AL2 implement eight SST39SF040-70-4I-NHE PLCC32 devices with private outputs and bank muxes. The runner reconstructs every ALU word from eight programming files; the archived Batronix support list names the exact part and BA005 adapter. Complete physical procurement, socket/passive/footprint selection, programming and full-device readback. AL1's obsolete M27C322-100F1 remains a legacy timing-study reference.

risks.title: Clock phase and loading
risks.action: C1 is a separate KiCad counted-clock candidate: 8 MHz / 8, 375 ns nominal separation, opposite-edge staging, complete-cycle stop and latched single-step. SQ1 adds retained HALT/request arbitration and tests resume/STEP. C1's narrowest internal margin remains 2.30 ns under allocated loads/jitter. Complete debounce/supervisor integration and qualify slew, jitter, PCB capacitance, metastability and receiver reset behavior before replacing the active RC-clock baseline.

risks.title: Non-arithmetic overflow contract
risks.action: V=0 outside signed arithmetic opcodes 3–15. The regenerated ROM matches the independent oracle in all 2,097,152 complete words; controller comparisons include V.

risks.title: Complete instruction and system coverage
risks.action: Extend exhaustive handler checks to every addressing mode, conditional control flow, memory/IO and boundary behaviour; then compare a complete hardware model against the reviewed instruction contract.

risks.title: Controller and full-machine integration
risks.action: Review current FD1/BP1/BL1 results for private DATA routing, distributed clock/reset, logical backplane and CPU-executed ROM loading. Qualify physical loading, flash/ROM programming and readback, supply/reset and the exact oscillator; implement external display hardware. Invalid-opcode fail-stop behaviour for zero-filled unused words remains undefined.

risks.title: Layouts and electrical release review
risks.action: Complete routing; verify pad-net equivalence, ERC/DRC, fanout, decoupling, bus contention, power distribution and signal integrity.

risks.title: Physical calibration
risks.action: Measure clock/data/OE paths on an instrumented prototype and repeat diagnostics at the agreed voltage, temperature and frequency limits.

risks.title: Review migration boundary
risks.action: Native KiCad library import now independently checks pin geometry, aliases, units, rotations/mirrors and hidden supplies. All 1,134 pin groups, including singletons, agree across seven sheets. Source wire/placement/scalar-label parsing remains shared, original annotation graphics are excluded, and fabrication review remains outstanding.

risks.title: Reset threshold and power ramp
risks.action: Manual reset no longer shorts the MCP100 push-pull output; its indicator is separately driven and the settled logic passes. The existing 450 grade can release below 4.75 V. Qualify rail-rise/brownout behavior, supervisor threshold/delay, button debounce and receiver reset recovery/removal. A delay measured from threshold crossing is not necessarily a delay from oscillator-valid supply.

risks.title: Controller peripheral integration
risks.action: SP1/MA1 implement the early MAR transfer with PH1 snapshots and dedicated PC/SP links; ME1 adds protected ROM/SRAM and registered IO. Review the 13-profile candidate results and complete-demo evidence at the IO connector model. Idle-only debounced RESUME, receiver reset and global clock/control loading need qualification.

risks.title: Shared DATA overload and private-link qualification
risks.action: The baseline shared DATA audit remains 90–100 pF before routing and fourteen output pins. FD1 replaces it with continuously driven private sources, mux selection and seven receive branches. Its 324-link audit requires one driver and at most the declared 50 pF allocation per link. Verify actual routing, mating connectors, capacitance over temperature and slew; each 10 pF link allowance covers the entire interconnect.

risks.title: PC shared-bus load and integration
risks.action: PC1 implements four HCT161 counters with falling-edge staged carries and reset-inhibited outputs. Resolve the DATA load: 20 pF of counter inputs plus 50 pF allocated external load exceeds the buffer's 50 pF test condition, before unbounded inactive-output capacitance. Qualify global bus handover, controller timing, reset and PC-to-MAR hold. Candidate simulations at datasheet delays do not close these gaps.

risks.title: Structural circuit wiring
risks.action: The 33 remaining ALU inputs are wired or terminated. Seven sheets now have no findings in the bounded supply/unit/input/direct-family audit. ALU operand and flag storage use common PH3; the disabled old clock buffer has terminated inputs. All previously missing power/spare units are present. This does not establish load, timing or power-integrity qualification.

risks.title: Memory transition timing
risks.action: ME1 models ROM/RAM access, SRAM write cycle/pulse/address/data timing and registered IO. Qualify the SRAM private bus: its 23 pF numeric allocation omits inactive AHCT output capacitance, disable timing is specified at 5 pF and capacitance at 25 C. Reset-interrupted writes, physical address hazards, slew and global bus handover remain open.

risks.title: ALU electrical release and shared loading
risks.action: AL2 retains PH1 result snapshots and synchronous PH3 A/flag capture with FR1 flash. Its isolated shared-DATA stage retains the 90–100 pF receiver budget; the separate FD1 distribution stage uses private links. Qualify actual load, slew, flash startup/readback, supply/reset and PCB skew. The numbered Adam Tech socket alternative requires a separate 1.10 mm-hole footprint; it does not qualify the installed 0.80 mm Assmann-derived footprint.

risks.title: 4 MHz distribution target and physical backplane
risks.action: The bounded FD1 interval review retains 46 paths and explicitly rejects 8 MHz. Source an exact active 4 MHz oscillator, qualify reset assertion/release and brownout behaviour, and complete the BP1 physical backplane. The logical 81-header drawing has no routed layout. Preserve pin numbering and PC1 J1 pin 10 ground strap; measure whole-link capacitance and propagation before physical acceptance.
